post.caption: The Medici Venus had golden hair. This marble copy of a Greek bronze is about 2,000 years old. Recorded in Rome in 1638, she moved to Florence in 1677. Visitors in the 1700s wrote that her hair was gilded. By the 1800s, the gold was gone, perhaps scrubbed off on purpose. In 2012, restorers found gold leaf over a red base layer. Her lips carried red cinnabar, and her earlobes were pierced for jewelry. Under the wave her dolphin rides, they found Egyptian blue. She is 153 centimeters tall and kept in the Uffizi.
